2026 SPY backtest

Historical simulation · January 2 to November 13, 2026 · 219 sessions

We tested a rule for buying SPY after its price fell below its recent average. The run that sets the order size before the next session’s open returned +2.37% over the period.

These are simulated results from historical SPY prices. Actual trading results can differ.

Why fill timing matters

The original report uses the final closing price to make the decision and assumes the order fills at that close. That gives the simulation a price it could only know after the market closed. In the next-open run, signals and order sizes are set after the close. Orders fill at the next open if there is enough cash.

Rules and costs

The rule buys when SPY closes more than two standard deviations below its 20-session moving average. It exits on a return to that average or when the closing price crosses the trailing stop.

Position sizing uses a 2% risk budget and a stop distance of 2.5 times the 20-session average true range. The simulation uses no leverage.

Both runs start with USD 100,000 in simulated capital. Each order includes a USD 1 commission and 0.01% slippage. Ending values include open positions. Dividends and interest are excluded.

From rule to test

A bot needs clear rules about when it trades, how much it can trade, and when it should stop.

Define the limits

Decide how large a position can be, and what the bot should do if a price is missing or an order is rejected.

Test with realistic assumptions

Historical tests and simulations can show how rules respond to different prices and costs. Future results can differ.
